modes.cue_notes: From plank, bend the elbows straight back at roughly a 90-degree angle, hugging them close to the ribs rather than flaring outward. Keep the body in one plank-length line — no dropping the hips, no lifting them — and hover a few inches above the mat. Gaze slightly forward, shoulders no lower than elbow height to protect the shoulder joint.

notes: One of the most commonly misaligned vinyasa transitions; shallow bends and elbow flare are frequent teaching points. Beginners are usually cued to lower knees-chest-chin instead of a full hover.

breathing_cues.entering: Exhale as you shift weight forward and bend the elbows to lower halfway, keeping the descent controlled rather than a drop.
breathing_cues.holding: This is typically a single-breath transition; if pausing, breathe shallowly and evenly, keeping the core engaged.
breathing_cues.exiting: Inhale to press forward and up into upward-facing dog, rolling over the toes, or lower fully to the mat to rest.

modifications.name: Knees-Chest-Chin
modifications.description: Lower the knees to the mat first, then lower chest and chin toward the floor while keeping elbows hugged in, reducing load while learning the bend pattern.

modifications.name: Blocks Under Shoulders
modifications.description: Place yoga blocks under the shoulders to limit the depth of the lower and protect against collapsing too far.
